sections.label: Unclaimed money and foreign law experts
sections.summary: It introduces a framework for unclaimed client and intervention money and a registration category for non-practising foreign law experts in the SICC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Second, it introduces a framework to deal with unclaimed client money and brings unclaimed intervention money within the same framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Third, it introduces a registration category for non-practising foreign law experts to appear in the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) to make submissions on matters of foreign law.

sections.label: Unclaimed Money Fund administration
sections.summary: A new Unclaimed Money Fund will be maintained and administered by the Law Society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A new Unclaimed Money Fund (UM Fund) will be maintained and administered by the Law Society.

sections.label: Six-year limitation period
sections.summary: New sections provide a six-year limitation period from the Law Society's approval of the transfer, after which rights and claims are extinguished.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The new sections 70K(4) and 70L(1) provide a six-year limitation period, commencing from the date the Law Society approves the transfer of the unclaimed client moneys, for actions or claims to recover the transferred unclaimed client money.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: After six years, any rights the client may have against the lawyer in relation to the unclaimed client money, or any statutory claim a claimant may have against the Law Society, will be extinguished.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This is so that there will be clarity and certainty for the lawyers and law practices who transfer unclaimed client money into the UM Fund, especially for those who do so with a view towards retirement.

sections.label: Intervention money transferred to UM Fund
sections.summary: Clause 31 amends the Act so intervention money unclaimed for six years in the special account goes to the UM Fund, not the Compensation Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 31 of the Bill amends the current Act to provide for intervention money that has been unclaimed for six years in the special account to be transferred to the UM Fund instead of the Compensation Fund.

sections.label: SICC cases heard to date
sections.summary: SICC has heard 17 cases with diverse subject matters and parties from jurisdictions including Australia, Japan, Hong Kong, the UAE, India and Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To date, SICC has heard 17 cases, with diverse subject matters, including banking and finance, shipbuilding, construction, investment and involving parties from jurisdictions, such as Australia, Japan, Hong Kong, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), India and Indonesia.

sections.label: Online professional conduct test for solicitors
sections.summary: Solicitors practising litigation will need to complete a short online test on professional conduct rules and declare it before applying for or renewing practising certificates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The intention is to prescribe that solicitors who practise in the area of litigation will need to complete a short online test on professional conduct rules administered by the Law Society and declare that they have done the test before applying for or renewing their practising certificates.

sections.label: Bill clauses on Law Society
sections.summary: Clause 19 widens use of interest and capital, clause 17 credits penalty sums to the Law Society, and clause 30 allows group law practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 19 of the Bill makes amendments to provide Council with greater flexibility to use such interest, dividends and other accretions of capital towards a wider range of worthwhile causes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Third, clause 17 of the Bill allows penalty sums which are collected from solicitors who fail to vote at the annual election of Law Society Council members to be credited to the Law Society, instead of the Compensation Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Fifth, clause 30 of the Bill allows Singapore law practices which are structured as law corporations and limited liability law partnerships to form a group law practice.

sections.label: Senior judge as Tribunal President
sections.summary: Clause 25 clarifies that a senior judge of the Supreme Court can be appointed to sit as President of the Disciplinary Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Sixth, clause 25 of the Bill clarifies that a senior judge of the Supreme Court of Singapore can be appointed to sit as the President of the Disciplinary Tribunal.

sections.label: Bill and wholly-owned subsidiaries
sections.summary: The Bill provides for wholly-owned subsidiaries letting the Law Society use separate legal entities to perform functions and activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill furthers their efforts and the legal profession's contribution to society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It provides for wholly-owned subsidiaries which would allow the Law Society to make use of separate legal entities to perform functions and activities.

sections.label: Regulating group law practices
sections.summary: Clause 30 introduces a new Division 5 regulating group practices in Singapore by Singapore and foreign law practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 30 introduces a new Division 5 that would regulate group practices in Singapore by Singapore and foreign law practices.

sections.label: Fund use and claim time
sections.summary: New section 70J(3)(b) allows use for pro bono services, and claims against the Fund are allowed up to six years after transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The new section 70J(3)(b) in clause 18 provides that it can be used for "pro bono services provided by the Law Society or by any wholly-owned subsidiary of the Society".

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Claims against the Fund are also allowed up to six years after the transfer, after which the Society still retains the discretion to pay part or whole of the amount being claimed.

sections.label: Penalty paid to Law Society
sections.summary: Clause 17 amends section 50 so a lawyer's penalty for failing to vote in council elections is paid to the Law Society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, clause 17 of the Bill proposes to amend section 50 of the Act to allow for the penalty paid by any lawyer for failing to vote in council elections to be paid to the Law Society and not the Compensation Fund.

sections.label: Purpose of change and monies
sections.summary: Asks the purpose of the change and whether monies directed to the Society will also be used for similar worthy causes serving public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In these circumstances, what is the purpose behind the change, and will the monies directed to the Society be also used for similar worthy causes to serve public interest?

sections.label: New UM Fund establishment
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a new UM Fund for transferring unclaimed client or intervention monies, to be paid into the Fund and vest in the Law Society absolutely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill introduces the establishment of a new UM Fund to allow for the transfer of unclaimed client or intervention monies to be paid into the Fund and to vest in the Law Society absolutely.

sections.label: Efforts to contact rightful owners
sections.summary: Asks what can ensure the Law Society expends sufficient efforts to contact rightful owners before using monies for pro bono services, noting MOF's statement on returning unclaimed monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the context of Government agencies, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) had made a statement that all Government agencies, including Statutory Boards, are required to make all reasonable efforts to return unclaimed monies to the rightful owners promptly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This being the case, what can be done to ensure that the Law Society expends sufficient efforts to contact the rightful owners of these monies before it decides to use these monies for pro bono services?

sections.label: Mandatory penalty wording change
sections.summary: The amendment to section 88(1) makes imposing a penalty, warning and/or reprimand mandatory by changing "may give" to "must give", and asks why.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Significantly, the amendment to section 88(1) proposes to make the imposition of a penalty, warning and/or reprimand mandatory by changing the wording to "must give" from the original "may give".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The question is, why are we changing from a "may" to a "must"?

sections.label: Section 88(3) consistency question
sections.summary: Asks the Senior Minister of State to clarify how section 88(3) is consistent with the mandatory imposition under section 88(1).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify how section 88(3) is consistent with the mandatory imposition under section 88(1)?

sections.label: Right to be heard on measures
sections.summary: Asks the Senior Minister of State to clarify whether a practitioner has the right to be heard before Council imposes remedial measures on him, in the same spirit of fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify whether a practitioner also has the right to be heard before Council imposes remedial measures on him in the same spirit of fairness?

sections.label: UM Fund and lawyer liability
sections.summary: The issue is resolved by the UM Fund, but section 70K(4) means a six-year wait before the lawyer is discharged from liability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The issue is now resolved with the introduction of the UM Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I appreciate the effort in calibrating the provisions of this new section to be fair to the lawyer, the Law Society as well as the client, especially if eventually he or she does show up and claim the monies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that the effect of the proposed sections 70K(3) and 70K(4) is that the lawyer may potentially face a claim from a client that resurfaces within six years from the time the unclaimed money is transferred to the Law Society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In these circumstances, may I seek clarification on the intent of section 70K(4) as there would be a wait of six years before the lawyer is discharged and free from any liability?

sections.label: UM Fund monies usage
sections.summary: Monies in the UM Fund may be used to fund, among other things, pro bono services provided by the Law Society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The final point I wish to raise is on the usage of the monies in the UM Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that the monies forming part of the Fund may be used to fund, amongst other things, pro bono services provided by the Law Society.

sections.label: Remedial measures for lawyers
sections.summary: Remedial measures let the Law Society Council deal with less serious disciplinary matters through training, counselling and rehabilitation, in addition to or instead of current options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The introduction of remedial measures under the disciplinary framework for lawyers allows the Law Society Council to have a wide range of measures to deal with less serious disciplinary matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These remedial measures can be imposed in addition to or in lieu of the current options which are available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Such remedial measures may involve training, counselling and other means of rehabilitation.

sections.label: Remedial measures not on roll
sections.summary: Because the remedial measures are not punitive and aim at rehabilitation, they are not entered against the lawyer's name on the roll.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In line with the nature of the remedial measures which are not punitive and consistent with the objective of rehabilitating the lawyer, these are not entered against the name of the lawyer on the roll.

sections.label: Compensation Fund contributions and payouts
sections.summary: Practising lawyers contribute S$100 annually, about S$500,000 yearly; the fund held S$13 million at 31 March 2017 and paid out about S$500,000 over six years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: All practising lawyers have to make an annual contribution of S$100 to the Compensation Fund, bringing the total annual contribution to about S$500,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the financial year ending 31 March 2017, the balance in the Compensation Fund amounted to S$13 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Over the past six years, about S$500,000 was paid out from the Compensation Fund.

sections.label: Returning client money duty
sections.summary: The Ministry asked the Professional Conduct Council Secretariat to consider an express duty for lawyers to return client money without undue delay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To complement the framework, my Ministry has also written to the Secretariat of the Professional Conduct Council to ask them, to consider introducing in the Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules, an express duty for lawyers to take reasonable efforts to return client money without undue delay, once the money is no longer required for the purpose for which they are held.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Rather, the Act, as amended, expressly requires the money to be invested for use to fund pro bono services.

sections.label: Unclaimed client money recovery time limit
sections.summary: No action to recover transferred unclaimed client money may be brought after six years from the Law Society's approval of the transfer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To summarise, this section provides that no action to recover any transferred unclaimed client money may be brought – after the expiry of six years from the date when the Law Society approves the transfer – against, first, the solicitor or Singapore law practice that paid the transferred unclaimed client money into the UM Fund or, second, any solicitor or Singapore law practice that held the money on account of a client at any time before that money was paid into the Fund.
